text:
incidents-bot: PAGER ALERT: P0 - GPU memory surge and container restarts observed in runtime-pool-3 (us-west). Multiple containers restarted over last 5m, possible OOM during prefill. Runbook: <https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-oom|gpu-oom>. Paging oncall: @olivia

olivia: ack — I'm on it. Starting log collection and will check node/driver health.

devon: seeing repeated SIGKILL on runtime containers: kubelet reports container exited with code 137. grabbing pod logs now.

infra-bot: snapshot: pods with restarts: runtime-xyz-7cdf (3x), runtime-abc-4f2e (2x). dmesg shows "Out of memory: Killed process" and NV driver reports GPU memory alloc failure.

devon: logs (tail):
```
2026-03-15T11:22:14Z runtime ERROR: prefill.kv_cache_bytes=21.3GiB allocation failed: CUDA out of memory
2026-03-15T11:22:14Z runtime INFO: container exiting with status 137
2026-03-15T11:22:15Z kubelet INFO: Evicting pod runtime-xyz-7cdf
```

meredith: hypothesis: very large single-context prefill causing KV cache growth -> GPU OOM -> container restart. Could be long/promiscuous prompts hitting one customer or a burst of long-context tests. Recommend immediate mitigations: 1) route very long requests to smaller model variant, 2) enable prefill trimming for requests > 200k tokens, 3) cordon/replace the flapping node to avoid noisy neighbor.

olivia: taking action now — applying emergency routing rule to send requests with estimated_context_length > 200k to model-small-v1. Also enabling prefix trimming in runtime config for the affected pool. Applying cordon on node-uw3-21.

olivia: commands used:
```
# add routing rule
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/routing -d '{"match": "estimated_context_tokens > 200000", "route_to": "model-small-v1"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer **REDACTED**'

# enable trimming
kubectl -n runtime set configmap runtime-config --from-literal=prefill_trim_threshold=200000

# cordon node
kubectl cordon node-uw3-21
kubectl drain node-uw3-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

infra-bot: nodal health: node-uw3-21 shows GPU memory fragmentation and recent driver warnings. cordon successful, pods rescheduled to runtime-pool-1/2.

devon: after routing change and trimming, restart spike dropped. error rate for generation requests in affected routes went from ~12% to ~0.8% in the last 8 minutes. stats from metrics: failure_count: 240 -> 16, p50 latency stable.

olivia: customer impact assessment:~10k requests affected in 12-minute window; ~4 customers had noticeable errors (>5% of their requests) — two internal customers (staging), two production customers (acct-824, acct-190). I'll loop in CS.

emma-cs: thanks, pinging CSMs and initiating incident notification drafts. we should tell prod customers we applied a temporary routing mitigation and are investigating root cause; ETA for follow-up 2h.

samir: collecting driver/kernel info from crashed host:
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
Product Name : NVIDIA A100
FB Memory Usage
    Total                       : 40960 MiB
    Used                        : 38912 MiB
    Free                        : 2048 MiB
# dmesg tail
[  1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, pid=10234, Ch 00000040, Reason: Ecc Volatile Error
[  1234.568001] Out of memory: Kill process 10234 (runtime) score 123 or sacrifice child
```

meredith: good captures — we should also check for a recent runtime change (rollout) that might have altered KV growth patterns. devon, any deploys to runtime-pool-3 in the last 24h?

devon: one small config push 9h ago: adjusted batch sizing defaults and a kernel pin change. rolling back that kernel pin could be low-risk if we suspect kernel scheduling changed memory allocation behavior.

olivia: low-risk rollback queued to canary in 10m for runtime-pool-3, will monitor. can someone prepare a canary and rollback plan? @samir?

samir: I can run the canary. Plan: 1) rollback kernel pin on a single node, 2) run synthetic long-context workload for 15m, 3) if stable, roll to other nodes. expected impact minimal.

infra-bot: canary started on node-uw3-22. synthetic test: sending 100 requests with long-context templates.

samir: canary logs: no OOMs during 30m synthetic run. starting staged rollout to remaining nodes in pool-3 (1 node/minute).

olivia: metrics during staged rollout: error rate remains <1%. good.

devon: note for postmortem: add a dataset of offending requests (anonymized) and model-side checks to detect high-token prefill before allocation to avoid OOMs. Also consider an allocation cap so prefill allocation can fail gracefully and fall back to streaming-mode.

olivia: handing off monitoring and follow-ups to @samir for the next 2h (overnight). My oncall shift ends in 25m — I'll leave a checklist:
- Routing rule active (estimated_context_tokens >200k -> model-small-v1)
- Prefill trimming enabled in runtime-config
- Node-uw3-21 cordoned and under replacement
- Kernel pin rollback in-progress and being monitored
- CS notified (acct-824, acct-190) with temporary mitigation note
- Postmortem meeting scheduled at 2026-03-16T15:00 UTC

samir: taking over monitoring. I've got alert windows tightened and will watch for regressions. If anything spikes, escalate to oncall. thanks @olivia.

emma-cs: customer message drafted: "We identified transient GPU memory errors affecting long-context requests; we've applied temporary routing to a smaller model and trimming to reduce memory use. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a detailed postmortem. Apologies for the disruption." ready to send after final numbers from olivia/samir. :email:

incidents-bot: Incident P0 -> mitigated (reduced error rates and stabilized nodes). Postmortem owner: devon. Links: runbook, metrics dashboard, postmortem draft: <https://redwood/incidents/4159876543/postmortem-draft|postmortem>.

olivia: leaving detailed notes in the incident doc and moving to handoff. thanks team. :heart:
